nodes.label: Hooks reference
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Reference for hook events, configuration schema, JSON input/output, exit codes, async hooks, HTTP hooks, prompt hooks and MCP tool hooks. Hooks are user-defined shell commands, HTTP endpoints or LLM prompts executing automatically at points in Claude Code's lifecycle, and they run WHEREVER Claude Code runs — terminal, IDE extensions, Desktop and Claude Code on the web all fire the same events.

nodes.label: Hook events fall into three cadences
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Once per SESSION (`SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`); once per TURN (`UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `StopFailure`); and on every TOOL CALL inside the agentic loop (`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`) — except `EndConversation` calls, which skip both tool events. The page states this taxonomy in its overview and places only these events in a cadence; many other documented events (`Notification`, `SubagentStart`, `PreCompact`, `ConfigChange`, `InstructionsLoaded`, the directory and file events) are not assigned to one.

nodes.label: Configuration has exactly three levels of nesting
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Choose a HOOK EVENT (the lifecycle point), add a MATCHER GROUP to filter when it fires, then define one or more HOOK HANDLERS to run when matched. The page uses those three terms precisely; 'hook' alone refers to the general feature.

nodes.label: How a hook resolves — matcher, then if, then handler
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: The event fires and Claude Code sends the event JSON to the handler — on stdin for a `command` hook, as the POST body for an `http` hook; the `matcher` checks the tool name and activates the group; the optional `if` condition narrows further and decides whether the handler runs at all (for `command` hooks, avoiding spawn overhead); the handler runs and prints a decision; Claude Code acts on it.

nodes.label: A hook can deny, but staying silent does NOT approve
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Exit code 0 with no output means the hook has NO DECISION to report, so the tool call continues through the normal permission flow. Silence is abstention, not approval — the distinction that decides whether a permissive hook is a security hole.

nodes.label: The Bash examples require jq on PATH
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Every Bash example on the page that parses JSON input uses `jq`, so it must be installed and on PATH before any of them will work. A missing `jq` makes the hook fail in a way that looks like a hook-system problem.

nodes.label: On Windows each tool needs its own if handler
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: A matcher `Bash|PowerShell` covers both tools, but a single `if` rule matches only ONE tool's calls — so `Bash(rm *)` and `PowerShell(Remove-Item *)` each need a separate handler. The scripts run via `powershell.exe` with `-NoProfile` (fast start) and `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` (to run the local file).

nodes.label: Six places a hook can be defined, and what each scopes to
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `~/.claude/settings.json` (all your projects, not shareable); `.claude/settings.json` (one project, committable); `.claude/settings.local.json` (one project, gitignored); managed policy settings (organization-wide, admin-controlled); a plugin's `hooks/hooks.json` (while the plugin is enabled); and skill or agent frontmatter (while the component is active).

nodes.label: Cloud sessions do NOT read your local ~/.claude/settings.json
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: On Claude Code on the web, hooks come from the REPO and from your organization's server-managed settings. A hook that works locally because it lives in your user settings simply does not exist in a cloud session.

nodes.label: Hooks also fire inside subagents, carrying agent_id and agent_type
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Hooks from settings files, managed policy and plugins run inside subagents too: when a subagent calls a tool, `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` fire the same configured hooks as in the main conversation, and the input carries `agent_id` and `agent_type` to identify which subagent.

nodes.label: Hook entries MERGE across settings levels
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: User, project and local settings ADD their own hooks without removing managed ones, and `disableAllHooks` cannot disable managed hooks from outside managed settings. Unlike most scalar settings, a lower level cannot displace a higher one here.

nodes.label: allowManagedHooksOnly blocks user, project and plugin hooks
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: An enterprise control. Hooks from plugins FORCE-ENABLED in managed settings `enabledPlugins` are exempt from the block — so the setting is 'only what the org sanctioned', not 'only what is literally in managed settings'.

nodes.label: Two HTTP hook allowlists apply to every source
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `allowedHttpHookUrls`: when defined at ANY settings level, an HTTP hook runs only if its URL matches the MERGED allowlist. `httpHookAllowedEnvVars`: when defined, only listed environment variables are interpolated into hook headers. Both apply to managed policy hooks as well.

nodes.label: A matcher's SYNTAX decides whether it is a string or a regex
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `"*"`, `""` or omitted matches all. Only letters, digits, `_`, `-`, spaces, `,` and `|` means EXACT string(s) separated by `|` or `,`. ANY other character makes it an UNANCHORED JavaScript regular expression. So the same string can mean two different things depending on one character. That character set holds for every matcher-supporting event EXCEPT `FileChanged` and `StopFailure`, which use a narrower one.

nodes.label: A regex matcher is unanchored — Edit.* also matches NotebookEdit
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: It is tested with `RegExp.prototype.test`, which succeeds on a match ANYWHERE in the value. Wrap in `^` and `$` (as `^Edit$`) for a whole-string match. The default is broader than most authors intend.

nodes.label: Comma separators and hyphens have version floors
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Comma separators and surrounding-whitespace tolerance need v2.1.191+. HYPHENS in the exact-match set need v2.1.195+ — on earlier versions `code-reviewer` is an unanchored regex and ALSO fires for `senior-code-reviewer`, so anchor it as `^code-reviewer$` there. A silently broader match, not an error.

nodes.label: FileChanged and StopFailure use a NARROWER exact-match set
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Letters, digits, `_` and `|` only. A hyphen, space or comma in a matcher for those two events keeps it on the REGEX path, and only `|` separates alternatives. Every other matcher-supporting event accepts `|` or `,`.

nodes.label: Each event matches on a DIFFERENT field
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Tool events match the tool name; `SessionStart` matches how the session started (`startup`/`resume`/`clear`/`compact`/`fork`); `SessionEnd` why it ended; `Notification` the notification type; `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop` the agent type; `PreCompact`/`PostCompact` what triggered compaction; `ConfigChange` the config source; `StopFailure` the error type; `InstructionsLoaded` the load reason.

nodes.label: Ten events have NO matcher support and always fire
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `UserPromptSubmit`, `PostToolBatch`, `Stop`, `TeammateIdle`, `TaskCreated`, `TaskCompleted`, `WorktreeCreate`, `WorktreeRemove` and `MessageDisplay` (one table row), plus `CwdChanged` (a row of its own) — ten in all. A `matcher` added to one of these is SILENTLY IGNORED rather than rejected.

nodes.label: MCP tools match as mcp__<server>__<tool>, and the .* is required
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `mcp__memory__.*` matches all tools from the memory server. A bare `mcp__memory` contains only exact-match characters, so it is compared as an EXACT STRING and matches NO tool — a matcher that looks like a prefix and silently matches nothing.

nodes.label: Plugin-bundled MCP servers use a SCOPED tool name
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `mcp__plugin_<plugin-name>_<server-name>__<tool>`. A matcher written against the BARE server key never fires for these tools: a plugin `my-plugin` bundling server `db` exposes `query` as `mcp__plugin_my-plugin_db__query`, so the all-tools matcher is `mcp__plugin_my-plugin_db__.*`. The same scoped name must be used in an `if` field.

nodes.label: Five hook handler types
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `command` runs a shell command — or, when `args` is present, spawns the executable directly with no shell — receiving JSON on stdin and replying via exit code and stdout; `http` POSTs the JSON to a URL and reads the response body in the same format; `mcp_tool` calls a tool on an already-connected MCP server and treats its text output like stdout; `prompt` sends a single-turn evaluation to a Claude model; `agent` spawns a subagent that can use Read/Grep/Glob to verify before deciding (experimental).

nodes.label: All matching hooks run in PARALLEL, and duplicates run once
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Defining the same handler in more than one settings file runs it ONCE — but a plugin's or skill's copy of the same handler stays SEPARATE and runs too. So deduplication is scoped to settings files, not global.

nodes.label: Handlers run in the current directory with Claude Code's environment
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `$CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE` is `"true"` in remote web environments and UNSET in the local CLI, which is how a hook detects where it is running. From v2.1.199, `$CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID` carries the Remote Control session ID while a Remote Control connection is active.

nodes.label: The `if` field uses permission-rule syntax and holds exactly ONE rule
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `"Bash(git *)"` runs when any subcommand matches `git *`; `"Edit(*.ts)"` only for TypeScript files. There is NO `&&`, `||` or list syntax — multiple conditions mean multiple handlers. It is evaluated ONLY on tool events; on any other event a hook with `if` set NEVER RUNS.

nodes.label: Timeout defaults differ per handler type AND per event
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: 600s for `command`/`http`/`mcp_tool`, 30s for `prompt`, 60s for `agent`. `UserPromptSubmit` lowers the command default to 30 and `MessageDisplay` to 10. `SessionEnd` hooks share a 1.5-SECOND BUDGET, raised to match a longer per-hook `timeout` up to 60 seconds.

nodes.label: `once` is honored ONLY in skill frontmatter
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `once: true` runs the hook once per session then removes it — but it is IGNORED in settings files and in agent frontmatter. Setting it in the wrong place fails silently rather than erroring.

nodes.label: statusMessage customizes the spinner while a hook runs
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: A display-only field, but the only thing that tells a user WHY the session appears to be waiting during a slow hook.

nodes.label: Exec form vs shell form is decided by the presence of `args`
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: With `args`, `command` is resolved as an executable and spawned DIRECTLY with no shell — each element is one argument exactly as written, and apostrophes, `$` and backticks pass through verbatim. Without `args`, the string goes to a shell (`sh -c`, Git Bash, or PowerShell) which tokenizes, expands variables and interprets pipes, `&&`, redirects and globs.

nodes.label: Use exec form for ANY hook referencing a path placeholder
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Because each `args` element is passed as one argument with NO QUOTING, a path with spaces cannot break it. In shell form every placeholder must be wrapped in double quotes by hand. Omit `args` only when you genuinely need pipes or `&&`.

nodes.label: On Windows, exec form cannot run .cmd or .bat shims
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `command` must resolve to a real executable such as a `.exe`. The `.cmd`/`.bat` shims npm, npx and eslint install in `node_modules/.bin` are not executables. Invoke the underlying script with `node` instead — `"command": "node", "args": [".../eslint.js"]` — which works on every platform because `node.exe` is a real binary.

nodes.label: A bare exec-form command containing whitespace is a logged warning
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: In exec form `command` is the executable name or path ONLY. A bare name with whitespace alongside `args` makes Claude Code log a warning because the spawn will fail — there is no executable named `node script.js`. An absolute path containing spaces is a single valid executable and does not trigger it.

nodes.label: Three path placeholders, exported as environment variables too
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` (the project root, also set for stdio MCP servers and plugin LSP servers); `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` (the plugin's install directory, which CHANGES ON EACH UPDATE); `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` (the plugin's persistent data directory, for state that must survive updates). All three are also exported to the spawned process.

nodes.label: ${user_config.*} substitutes in EXEC FORM ONLY
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: A shell-form plugin hook whose `command` references `${user_config.*}` FAILS with an error rather than running. Read `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY>` instead, or set `args` to switch to exec form. Before v2.1.207 shell-form commands substituted it too.

nodes.label: async runs in the background; asyncRewake wakes Claude on exit 2
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `async: true` runs without blocking. `asyncRewake: true` implies async AND wakes Claude on exit code 2, showing the hook's stderr — or stdout if stderr is empty — as a system reminder, so Claude can react to a long-running background failure.

nodes.label: HTTP hook fields and the env-var interpolation gate
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `url` is required; `headers` values support `$VAR` / `${VAR}` interpolation, but ONLY variables listed in `allowedEnvVars` are resolved — references to unlisted variables become EMPTY STRINGS. `allowedEnvVars` is required for any interpolation to work at all.

nodes.label: MCP tool hooks call an already-connected server
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `server` (the scoped `plugin:<plugin>:<server>` name for a plugin-bundled server, not the bare key), `tool`, and optional `input` supporting `${path}` substitution from the hook's JSON such as `"${tool_input.file_path}"`. The hook NEVER triggers an OAuth or connection flow — an unconnected server or an `isError: true` result is a non-blocking error.

nodes.label: SessionStart and Setup fire BEFORE MCP servers connect
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: So an `mcp_tool` hook on either event should expect the 'not connected' error on first run. The handler type is available on every event, but not usefully on those two.

nodes.label: Prompt and agent hooks take `prompt` and optional `model`
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `$ARGUMENTS` is the placeholder for the hook input JSON, escaped with a backslash for literal text (`\$1.00` renders as `$1.00`). `model` defaults to a fast model.

nodes.label: Skills and subagents can define hooks in frontmatter
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Same configuration format, but scoped to the component's LIFETIME and cleaned up when it finishes. All events are supported, and for subagents a `Stop` hook is automatically CONVERTED to `SubagentStop`, since that is the event that actually fires.

nodes.label: A project subagent's frontmatter hooks require workspace trust (v2.1.218)
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: They run only after you accept the trust dialog for the folder the agent file came from. Before v2.1.218 these hooks could run from folders you had NOT trusted.

nodes.label: /hooks is a READ-ONLY browser showing each hook's source
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: It lists every event with a count, drills into matchers, and shows each handler's full command, prompt or URL, labeled `[type]` plus a source: User / Project / Local Settings, Plugin Hooks, Session Hooks (in-memory for this session), or Built-in Hooks. To change anything you edit the JSON or ask Claude.

nodes.label: disableAllHooks is all-or-nothing and respects the managed hierarchy
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: There is NO way to disable an individual hook while keeping it configured. And `disableAllHooks` set in user, project or local settings cannot disable MANAGED hooks — only the managed level can.

nodes.label: Hooks run without a controlling terminal (v2.1.139)
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: On macOS and Linux they run in their own session; the process and its children cannot open `/dev/tty` or send escape sequences directly to the interface, and Windows has no `/dev/tty` at all. Surface a message with `systemMessage`, or a notification/title/bell with `terminalSequence`.

nodes.label: The common input fields a hook receives
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `session_id`; `prompt_id` (a UUID matching the OpenTelemetry `prompt.id`, absent until first input, v2.1.196+); `transcript_path`; `cwd`; `permission_mode`; `effort` (an object with `level`); and `hook_event_name`. Inside a subagent, `agent_id` and `agent_type` are added.

nodes.label: transcript_path LAGS the in-memory conversation
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: It is written asynchronously and may not yet include the current turn's most recent messages when a hook fires. A hook needing the turn's final assistant text must use `last_assistant_message` on `Stop`/`SubagentStop` rather than reading the transcript.

nodes.label: The Manual permission mode arrives as "default", never "manual"
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: So scripts matching `"default"` keep working. A deliberate compatibility choice that makes the label and the wire value differ.

nodes.label: There is NO $CLAUDE_MODEL environment variable
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Only `SessionStart` hooks can receive a `model` field, and it is not guaranteed present. A hook inherits `$ANTHROPIC_MODEL` if you set it in your shell, but that value does NOT change when you switch models with `/model` mid-session. Separately, Claude Code REMOVES every `OTEL_*` exporter variable from any subprocess it spawns, including hooks.

nodes.label: Exit 0 / exit 2 / anything else
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Exit 0 = success, and stdout is parsed for JSON — JSON is processed ONLY on exit 0. Exit 2 = blocking error: stdout and any JSON in it are IGNORED and stderr is fed back to Claude as the error. Any OTHER code is a non-blocking error for most events; the action proceeds with a `<hook name> hook error` notice showing the first stderr line.

nodes.label: Exit code 1 does NOT block — use exit 2
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Claude Code treats 1 as a non-blocking error and proceeds, even though 1 is the conventional Unix failure code. A policy-enforcing hook must use `exit 2`. The one exception is `WorktreeCreate`, where ANY non-zero code aborts creation.

nodes.label: Exit 2 with schema-invalid JSON still blocks (v2.1.214)
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Claude Code uses stderr as the blocking reason and records the validation failure in the debug log. BEFORE v2.1.214 that combination was treated as a non-blocking error and the action PROCEEDED — a silent policy bypass on older versions.

nodes.label: Where stderr goes depends on the exit code
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Stderr from a hook exiting 0 goes to the DEBUG LOG ONLY — never the transcript, and Claude never sees it. To surface a warning to Claude from `PostToolUse`/`PostToolUseFailure`, exit 2 instead, which shows Claude the stderr even though the tool already ran.

nodes.label: Only three events treat stdout as context Claude can see
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `UserPromptSubmit`, `UserPromptExpansion` and `SessionStart`. For every other event stdout goes to the debug log but is NOT shown in the transcript.

nodes.label: Exit 2 blocks on some events and is inert on others
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Blocks: `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `UserPromptSubmit` (which also ERASES the prompt), `UserPromptExpansion`, `Stop`, `SubagentStop`, `TeammateIdle`, `TaskCreated` (rolls back creation), `TaskCompleted`, `ConfigChange` (except `policy_settings`), `PostToolBatch`, `PreCompact`, `Elicitation`, `ElicitationResult`, `WorktreeCreate`. Inert: the Post* events, `PermissionDenied`, `Notification`, `SessionStart`/`Setup`/`SubagentStart`, `SessionEnd`, `StopFailure`, `InstructionsLoaded`, `MessageDisplay` and the directory/file events.

nodes.label: An HTTP hook CANNOT signal a block through status codes
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: 2xx with an empty body = exit 0 with no output; 2xx plain text = the text is added as context; 2xx JSON = parsed as the normal JSON output schema; non-2xx, a connection failure or a timeout = a NON-BLOCKING error. To block, return 2xx with a JSON body carrying the decision fields.

nodes.label: Choose exit codes OR JSON, never both
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: JSON is processed only on exit 0; exit 2 discards it. Stdout must contain ONLY the JSON object — a shell profile that prints on startup breaks the parse.

nodes.label: Hook output strings are capped at 10,000 characters
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Including `additionalContext`, `systemMessage` and plain stdout. Output exceeding it is saved to a file and replaced with a preview plus the file path, the same way a large Bash result is handled.

nodes.label: The universal JSON output fields
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `continue` (default true; `false` stops Claude entirely and TAKES PRECEDENCE over any event-specific decision), `stopReason` (shown to the user, not to Claude), `suppressOutput`, `systemMessage`, and `terminalSequence`.

nodes.label: terminalSequence is restricted to a notification allowlist (v2.1.141)
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: OSC 0/1/2 (titles), OSC 9 (iTerm2/ConEmu/Windows Terminal/WezTerm, including `9;4` taskbar progress), OSC 99 (Kitty), OSC 777 (urxvt/Ghostty/Warp), and bare BEL. Anything else — CSI cursor/color, OSC palette, OSC 8 hyperlinks, OSC 52 clipboard, OSC 1337 — is REJECTED and the whole field ignored, so a hook can never corrupt an on-screen prompt.

nodes.label: additionalContext injects a system reminder at the hook's point
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Claude reads it on the next model request; it does not appear as a chat message. Where it lands depends on the event: at conversation start for `SessionStart`/`Setup`/`SubagentStart`; alongside the prompt for the UserPrompt events; next to the tool result for the tool events; at the end of the turn for `Stop`/`SubagentStop`, which CONTINUES the conversation so Claude can act on it.

nodes.label: Write additionalContext as FACTS, not as system instructions
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: 'The deployment target is production' reads as project information. Text framed as out-of-band system commands can trigger Claude's PROMPT-INJECTION DEFENSES, which makes Claude surface the text to you instead of treating it as context — a self-inflicted failure that looks like the hook being ignored.

nodes.label: Resumed sessions REPLAY saved context rather than re-running the hook
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: For mid-session events like `PostToolUse` or `UserPromptSubmit`, `--continue`/`--resume` replays the saved text for past turns, so timestamps or commit SHAs go STALE. `SessionStart` hooks do run again on resume with `source` set to `"resume"` (or `"fork"` with `--fork-session`), so they can refresh.

nodes.label: For instructions that never change, prefer CLAUDE.md
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: It loads without running a script and is the standard place for static project conventions. `additionalContext` is for environment STATE, conditional project rules, and external data — things a static file cannot know.

nodes.label: Four decision patterns, chosen by event
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: A top-level `decision: "block"` plus `reason` (the UserPrompt events, the Post* events, `Stop`/`SubagentStop`, `ConfigChange`, `PreCompact`); exit code or `continue: false` (`TeammateIdle`, `TaskCreated`, `TaskCompleted`); `hookSpecificOutput` (`PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `PermissionDenied`, the Elicitation events, `MessageDisplay`); and context-only (`SessionStart`, `Setup`, `SubagentStart`). Nine events have no decision control at all.

nodes.label: "block" is the ONLY value for a top-level decision
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: To allow the action, omit `decision` entirely or exit 0 with no JSON. There is no `"allow"` on this path.

nodes.label: Three events can REWRITE content rather than only allow or block
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `PreToolUse` uses `updatedInput` to replace a tool's arguments before it runs; `PermissionRequest` uses `updatedInput` inside its `decision` object; `PostToolUse` uses `updatedToolOutput` to replace the result. `UserPromptSubmit` CANNOT replace the prompt — it only injects `additionalContext` alongside it. For redaction, intercept `PreToolUse` outbound and `PostToolUse` inbound.

nodes.label: Not every event supports every handler type
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Thirteen events support ALL FIVE types (the tool events, `Stop`/`SubagentStop`, the UserPrompt events, the Task events, `TeammateIdle`, `PermissionRequest`/`PermissionDenied`, `PostToolBatch`). Fifteen support `command`/`http`/`mcp_tool` but NOT `prompt` or `agent`. `SessionStart` and `Setup` support only `command` and `mcp_tool` — no `http` either.

nodes.label: A prompt hook is a single LLM call returning a decision
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: It sends the hook input and your prompt to a Claude model — Haiku by default — the model responds with structured JSON, and Claude Code processes the decision automatically. No shell, no tools, one turn.

nodes.label: $ARGUMENTS is optional — the input is appended if absent
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: If the placeholder is not present in the prompt text, the hook input JSON is APPENDED to the prompt instead. So a prompt that forgets it still receives the data, just at the end.

nodes.label: The response schema is {ok, reason}
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `ok: true` allows; `ok: false` produces a `decision: "block"` and `reason` becomes the block reason and is REQUIRED. That two-field contract is the whole interface between the evaluating model and Claude Code.

nodes.label: continueOnBlock decides whether a block ends the turn
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: When the prompt returns `ok: false`, `continueOnBlock: true` feeds the reason back to Claude and CONTINUES the turn instead of stopping. It is implemented as `continue: true` on the resulting `decision: "block"`. Default is `false`.

nodes.label: What ok:false does varies sharply by event
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `Stop`/`SubagentStop`: the reason becomes Claude's next instruction and the turn continues. `PreToolUse`: the call is denied and by default the TURN ENDS (before v2.1.210 it continued). `PostToolBatch`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`UserPromptExpansion` end the turn REGARDLESS of `continue`. `PostToolUseFailure`/`TaskCreated` always continue. `TeammateIdle` stops the teammate by default.

nodes.label: ok:false has NO EFFECT on PermissionRequest or PermissionDenied
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: On `PermissionRequest` you must use a COMMAND hook returning `hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior: "deny"`. On `PermissionDenied` the only field read is `hookSpecificOutput.retry`, which prompt and agent hooks cannot set — they run and their output is DISCARDED. A prompt hook on either event is silently useless.

nodes.label: A Stop hook can check several conditions in one prompt
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: The documented example asks whether all requested tasks are complete, whether any errors need addressing, and whether follow-up work is needed, responding `{"ok": true}` to allow stopping or `{"ok": false, "reason": ...}` to continue. `SubagentStop` uses the identical format.

nodes.label: Agent hooks are EXPERIMENTAL — prefer command hooks in production
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Behavior and configuration may change in future releases. The docs say so explicitly and point production workflows at command hooks.

nodes.label: An agent hook is a multi-turn verifier with tool access
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Claude Code spawns a subagent with your prompt and the hook's JSON input; it can use Read, Grep and Glob to investigate; after UP TO 50 TURNS it returns a `{ok}` decision processed exactly like a prompt hook's. Default timeout 60s. Useful when verification requires inspecting real files or test output rather than the hook input alone.

nodes.label: An async hook CANNOT block or control Claude
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `decision`, `permissionDecision` and `continue` have no effect, because the action they would have controlled has already completed. `async` is available on `type: "command"` hooks ONLY.

nodes.label: Async output is delivered on the NEXT conversation turn
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: If the session is idle, the response waits for the next user interaction — except an `asyncRewake` hook exiting 2, which wakes Claude immediately even when idle. `additionalContext` reaches Claude; `systemMessage` is shown to you, not Claude.

nodes.label: In -p mode async hooks are KILLED at teardown
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Claude Code finalizes any still-running async hook with outcome `cancelled`. If the work must outlive a `claude -p` session, start a fully DETACHED process from the hook.

nodes.label: Async JSON is validated and bad fields are dropped (v2.1.202)
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Claude Code validates against the same output schema and DROPS any field with the wrong type — a `systemMessage` that is not a string, for example — rather than delivering it; `--debug` names each dropped field. Before v2.1.202 malformed async JSON could CRASH the session, and the crash RECURRED on every resume.

nodes.label: Each async firing is a separate process with no deduplication
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: There is no dedup across multiple firings of the same async hook, so a hook on a frequently-firing event spawns one background process per occurrence.

nodes.label: Async completion notifications are suppressed by default
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Enable verbose mode with Ctrl+O or start with `--verbose` to see them. So a silently-failing async hook looks like nothing happening.

nodes.label: Command hooks execute with your FULL user permissions
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: They can modify, delete or access any file your user account can. The docs carry this as an explicit warning: review and test every hook command before adding it to your configuration.

nodes.label: Five hook security practices
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Validate and sanitize inputs — never trust input data blindly; always quote shell variables (`"$VAR"`, not `$VAR`); block path traversal by checking for `..`; use absolute paths (in exec form `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` needs no quoting, in shell form wrap it in double quotes); and skip sensitive files such as `.env`, `.git/` and keys.

nodes.label: shell: powershell runs one hook under PowerShell on Windows
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Claude Code auto-detects `pwsh.exe` (PowerShell 7+) and falls back to `powershell.exe` for Windows PowerShell 5.1. It does not require `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL`, because hooks spawn PowerShell directly.

nodes.label: PowerShell placeholders are rewritten to ${env:NAME} (v2.1.198)
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}`, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` and `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` are rewritten in a PowerShell shell-form command whether it came from settings, a plugin or a skill. PowerShell resolves the value AFTER parsing, so it works inside double-quoted strings but NOT single-quoted ones. Before v2.1.198 the rewrite applied only to plugin hooks.

nodes.label: NEVER write bare $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR in a PowerShell hook
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: PowerShell parses it as an undefined LOCAL variable and resolves it to `$null`, leaving the script path without its project-root prefix. Claude Code does NOT rewrite that form — it logs a warning in the debug log instead, so the hook silently runs against the wrong path.

nodes.label: Hook execution details go to the debug log, not the terminal
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Which hooks matched, their exit codes and full stdout/stderr. Use `claude --debug-file <path>`, or `claude --debug` and read `~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt` — `--debug` does NOT print to the terminal. `CLAUDE_CODE_DEBUG_LOG_LEVEL=verbose` adds matcher counts and query matching.
